## File: `references/languages/javascript.md`

### Detection signals — JavaScript/TypeScript (Security: Identity & Access)

Detection signals only. They cite no standard. Report findings against the element IDs listed (defined in
`../standards/`). Passport, NextAuth/Auth.js, `jsonwebtoken`, `jose` and NestJS guard defaults aren't localized: judge
explicit code and settings only, and add a `localized-standard-gap` note when a decision depends on a default.

| Signal (API, setting or pattern) | Look in | Indicates | Element(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Router or app without auth middleware before protected routes; `app.use(passport.authenticate(...))` only on some routers | app setup, routers | No deny-by-default | ATZ-02 |
| Handler loading a record by `req.params.id` without checking the owner or tenant | handlers | IDOR | SEC-IA-02 elements (ATZ, T10) |
| `jwt.verify(token, key)` without `algorithms`; `jwt.decode` used for trust; `ignoreExpiration: true` | auth code | JWT not verified properly | JWT-01 and the other SEC-IA-03 elements |
| `express-session` options: `secure: false`, `httpOnly: false`, no `sameSite`, no `name`, no `store` | app setup | Weak session cookie / memory store | NDA-01, NDA-02, SES-04, SES-05, SES-06 |
| `csurf` dependency; state-changing routes with session auth and no CSRF token | `package.json`, routes | CSRF | NDA-04 |
| Login route without `rate-limiter-flexible`/`express-rate-limit`/lockout | auth routes | Brute force | NDA-03, ATN-12 |
| `bcrypt.hash(pw, <10)`, `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(password)`, `md5(password)` | user code | Weak password hashing | PWS-01 |
| `localStorage.setItem('token', …)`, `sessionStorage` for tokens | front-end files | Token in web storage | SES-17 |
| `req.session.regenerate` absent after login | auth code | No session rotation | SES-11 |

## File: `references/standards/node-identity-access.md`

*Load rule: NDA-01…05. Load when language `javascript` is detected.*

### Node.js / Express identity and access guidance — localized summary

- Applies when language `javascript` is detected and the code runs on Node.js (server code, not browser bundles);
  Express rows need `express` as a dependency. 
- Level: `MUST` where the source says must/must not/never/do not or gives an unqualified imperative; `SHOULD` for
  should/recommended/encouraged/"consider". **(Default)** marks an element that states library behaviour or a default;
  cite the OWASP element that is violated and name this element in the recommendation. Defaults stated here are the
  only Node.js/Express defaults a worker may rely on. Severity rules are in `../../SKILL.md`.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NDA-01 | SHOULD | Session cookies set `httpOnly`, `secure` and `sameSite` (`express-session`/`cookie-session` `cookie` options) and don't use the default session cookie name; `trust proxy` is set when TLS terminates at a proxy. | `session({ cookie: { secure: false } })`; no `name` (default `connect.sid`); `httpOnly: false` | SEC-IA-05 |
| NDA-02 | MUST (Default) | `express-session`'s default in-memory store isn't designed for production; production uses a shared session store. `cookie-session` keeps the whole session in a client-visible cookie, so it holds only small, non-sensitive data. | `session({ … })` with no `store` in production code; tokens or roles kept in `cookie-session` | SEC-IA-05 |
| NDA-03 | SHOULD | Login is protected against brute force: blocking by consecutive failures per username+IP and by total failures per IP over a long period (`rate-limiter-flexible`, `express-brute`, account lockout). | login route with no limiter or lockout | SEC-IA-09 |
| NDA-04 | MUST | Cookie-authenticated state changes use the framework's CSRF defence or maintained token middleware; the archived `csurf` package isn't used, and `SameSite` isn't the only mitigation. | `csurf` in `dependencies`; POST/PUT/DELETE routes behind session auth with no CSRF token check | SEC-IA-05 |
| NDA-05 | SHOULD | Access is granted by least privilege through roles or ACLs checked on the server (e.g. role middleware on each protected router). | admin routes guarded only by a client-side flag | SEC-IA-02 |
